title: Coffee latte
prompt: Instagram post announcing a new oat milk latte at a neighborhood coffee shop, cozy, warm morning light
outcomeNote: The glass is huge relative to the window and plant, and evenly front-lit while the scene is strongly backlit by the sun. Its base rests on the top edge of the brown panel instead of on a table or sill, so it reads as a floating sticker rather than part of the cozy scene.

provenance.model: Sonnet 5.5 (art director and fixer), Opus 5.5 (judge), FLUX.1 schnell (images), BiRefNet on Replicate (cutouts)
notes: Cutouts were measured during the run against the backdrop color of the uncut image, which the run didn't keep, so some cutout-quality warnings can't be reproduced now.

plan.concept: A warm, sunlit café table with a single oat milk latte as the hero, soft morning window light and creamy tones that make the new drink feel like a cozy ritual.

copy.headline: Meet the Oat Milk Latte
copy.subheading: New on the menu, made for slow mornings

layouts.name: headline top, latte center on table
layouts.rationale: Headline sits in the calm upper area while the latte rests on a wooden table below, giving a clear top-to-bottom read.

layouts.name: text panel bottom, latte above
layouts.rationale: A solid translucent panel at the bottom holds all copy with strong contrast, letting the latte and window light dominate the upper area.

edits.reason: Headline bottom to 865 matches CTA bottom edge.

steps.summary: Enlarge the glass and lower it so its base rests on the dark panel edge, with a stronger contact shadow.

edits.reason: Keep centered (x=540 center) and drop base to the panel top at ~617

steps.summary: Move the product up so it clears the headline, enlarge it slightly, and center it exactly on the canvas axis.

edits.reason: Larger product for more attention, ending above the headline.
Center on the canvas axis and lift above the headline to remove the overlap.

judgments.summary: The latte glass looks pasted in and floats in front of the window instead of resting on a surface. Its flat front lighting also doesn't match the backlit morning scene. Text and CTA are clean, but the hero product integration needs work.

findings.description: The glass hovers mid-air against the window panes, with the street visible below its base and no table or sill under it. It also ends above the dark panel rather than sitting on it, so it reads as a sticker, not part of the scene.
The glass is evenly front-lit on a crisp studio cutout, while the scene is strongly backlit by low sun with a soft depth of field. The lighting and focus mismatch makes the composite obvious.

judgments.summary: The cutout is clean and the copy reads well, but the latte glass looks pasted onto the scene. It is oversized, flatly lit against strong backlight, and stands on the edge of the text panel rather than on a real surface.

findings.description: The glass is huge relative to the window and plant, and evenly front-lit while the scene is strongly backlit by the sun. Its base rests on the top edge of the brown panel instead of on a table or sill, so it reads as a floating sticker rather than part of the cozy scene.
The flat brown panel covers the lower half and hides the table and cup in the background photo. The bottom half feels heavy and disconnected from the warm window scene above.
